thread:
raj: quick async dump from this week's cross-family GPTQ bake. ran Llama3-13b, Mistral-8k, Qwen-34b under GPTQ4 and AWQ/INT8 variants. TL;DR: stable on most short-context tasks, but Qwen long-context + GPTQ shows reproducible kv-drift + runtime variance. run id: bake-2026-03-19-r1

alex: nice. short summary numbers?

raj: TL;DR numbers (median across eval shards):
- Llama3-13b GPTQ-4: MMLU delta ~ -0.9% vs fp16, perplexity +5.8%
- Mistral-8k GPTQ-4: MMLU delta ~ -1.6%, codegen pass@1 down 1.2%
- Qwen-34b GPTQ-4: MMLU delta ~ -3.4%, longcontext codegen perplexity jump on >8k tokens workloads (up to +18%), reproduces across seeds.
- AWQ/int8 (per-family tuned): generally smaller accuracy deltas (~-0.3% to -0.8%) and much better longcontext stability for Qwen.

maria: can you paste the quant config used for GPTQ runs?

raj: sure, pasted the exact snippet used for all three families so we can compare:```
quant_backend: gptq
bits: 4
per_channel: true
act_ordering: true
clip_eps: 1e-3
calibration_samples: 256
block_size: 128
use_cached_kv_norm: false
```
note: for Qwen we initially used block_size 256 then dropped to 128 after divergence showed up.

eva: what does the kv-drift look like in logs? any stack trace or obvious ops?

raj: snippet from the eval-run logs where perplexity diverges around token 5120:```
[2026-03-19T14:02:21Z] model=qwen-34b-gptq4 step=5120 seq_len=8192 logp=-6.21 cached_kv_norm=0.00091
[2026-03-19T14:02:21Z] model=qwen-34b-gptq4 step=5121 seq_len=8192 logp=-18.47 cached_kv_norm=0.0372  <-- sudden jump
[2026-03-19T14:02:21Z] model=qwen-34b-gptq4 step=5122 seq_len=8192 logp=-19.01 cached_kv_norm=0.0421
```
looks like KV cache scale mismatch accumulates and suddenly amplifies logits. present across GPUs and seeds.

tim: infra note: observed slightly higher fp32-to-fp16 conversion jitter when packed ops went through CUTLASS fallback on our A100s. not sure if related.

ci-bot: full artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-bakes/bake-2026-03-19-r1/{qwen,mistral,llama}/metrics.json (sha256: ab12...) :white_check_mark:

maria: did you try per-channel scale re-estimation during serving (online rounding) or asymmetric quantization?

raj: quick experiments: per-channel recalibrate every 1024 tokens reduced drift by ~30% but didn't eliminate it. asymmetric int8 (AWQ-style) removed the catastrophic jumps entirely on Qwen at modest latency cost.

alex: so practical recommendation for rollout?

raj: proposed deployment profiles for now:
- Hosted (low-latency public): use AWQ/int8 for Qwen-34b and Mistral-8k; GPTQ-4 only for Llama3-13b where regression within acceptable bounds.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity customers wanting max throughput): offer GPTQ-4 as "best-effort" for Llama family with explicit QA gate; for Qwen provide AWQ as default and GPTQ behind opt-in + canary with strict longcontext eval set.
- Private/on-prem: provide both but surface a per-model "stability index" and require KV-alignment test in onboarding flow.

maria: can we add a regression alert to Console so any PR that increases longcontext perplexity >10% triggers rollback?

raj: yes — filed GH issue #1428 to add longcontext regressions to the evalsuite and hook to rollout policy.

eva: curious re: FP8 — you tried any fp8-ish dynamic range tricks?

raj: quick FP8 probe on Mistral: numerical under/overflow on a few layernorm gamma scales; Mistral's high-layer scaling makes FP8 risky without per-channel rescale. FP8 latency win is nice but accuracy and stability not production-ready yet.

tim: ops ask — if we default Qwen to AWQ in Hosted, what's the perf delta?

raj: median token latency: Qwen-34b fp16 32ms, AWQ/int8 22ms, GPTQ-4 18ms (but with occasional spikes on longcontext). throughput: AWQ slightly worse than GPTQ due to per-token dequant overhead but more stable tail latency.

maria: next action items?

raj: short list: 
- add KV-alignment microbench to onboarding (maria)
- bake a targeted GPTQ pass with per-channel rescale patch (raj + eva)
- AWQ perf tuning to reduce dequant overhead (tim + eng-runtime)
- add longcontext regression gate to Console + evalsuite (alex)

alex: thanks — if anyone wants the raw eval shards I can hand them off. ping me. :folded_hands:

maria: cool thread. marking for follow-up in next quant sync. :calendar:

eva: adding a note — when we re-run, include both seed=42 and seed=314 to catch nondeterministic drift.

tim: created a smoke canary job for bake-2026-03-19-r1 that runs every 6h against canary subset. job id: canary-4481239

raj: perfect. thanks all. closing thread but will post updated numbers after the per-channel rescale run. :rocket:
